source_text.Q-1042: MEDIUM, owner CI lane (follow-up of Q-1037, the next lever after sharding). Reported by the supervisor 2026-10-08. Evidence: ExUnit reports ~0.5 s average per test and ~66 min of cumulative test work per backend run (7.7k tests); a large share is believed to be the per-test tenant schema clone from tenant_template (CREATE SCHEMA ... LIKE tenant_template... for every table, see the LETFLOW_TENANT_FIXTURE setup/teardown log lines and the 'tenant_template_build' schemas): cost per test = DDL for every table of the template plus DROP SCHEMA CASCADE at teardown. NOT yet measured: step 1 is to instrument (time per clone, number of tables cloned, share of test time) on one partition, step 2 choose the lever: (a) clone only the tables the test needs, (b) share a read-only tenant across tests that do not mutate it (async-safe), (c) a pooled tenant per module with truncate-reset, (d) Postgres schema cloning via CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE or a faster mechanism; keep isolation guarantees (no cross-test leakage, the ISS-0410-class isolation bugs). Each step measured before/after; mutation proof that isolation still holds (a test that leaves data behind must not leak into the next). Overlap check 2026-10-08: Q-1037 is the umbrella; ISS-0410 (isolation failure, blocked) is background, not a duplicate.

task.description:
WF-03 Step 2 (fix design) for ISS-1042 / Q-1042 / GH #2381. DESIGN ONLY: produce the design artefact per your role file (.claude/agents/code-designer.md) and docs/agents/ conventions; no implementation code.

READ FIRST: docs/issues/ISS-1042.yaml (the full measured diagnosis, committed on this branch), and handoffs/WF03-ISS1042-20261012/step-01-issue-fixer.json result.summary. Then read test/support/tenant_fixture.ex and test/support/tenant_template.ex and the existing tests of both.

DESIGN TARGET (ISSUE-FIXER's recommendation, lever c refined): an opt-in, module-scoped pooled tenant with a dirty-table-only reset, default behaviour unchanged. Measured facts to design against: clone mean ~839 ms (50 tables, LIKE loop ~621 ms); full TRUNCATE of 57 tables 932-1055 ms (slower than a clone, so a full truncate is NOT acceptable); truncating a subset ~8 ms/table; probing all tables for rows ~3.6 ms. Highest-clone modules to adopt first: IdentityIdHardeningTest (114 clones), PromotionScopeTest (51), StoreTest (39).

THE DESIGN MUST SPECIFY, unambiguously enough to build from:
1. Public API (names, @specs, options) added to Letflow.TenantFixture / Letflow.Test.TenantTemplate, and how a module opts in (setup_all vs setup, ExUnit lifecycle, on_exit/teardown of the pooled schema, behaviour when a test in the module fails or times out mid-way).
2. The dirty-detection and reset algorithm: how 'dirty' is determined cheaply and correctly (e.g. probe each table for rows / xmin / pg_stat counters; justify the choice with the measured numbers), ordering vs FK constraints, sequence reset, seeded tables (event_type_registry, schema_migrations, template seed copy) that must be restored not emptied, triggers.
3. Public-schema state keyed to the tenant (the ISS-0410 class: Registration insert and any other public rows) and how the pooled design keeps those isolated or reset between tests, so there is no cross-test leakage.
4. Which tests MUST keep a fresh per-test clone (DDL/drop tests such as RegistryTenantSchemaMissingTest, TenantProvisioningTest, the 22 template: :replay sites) and how the default path stays byte-for-byte unchanged for them.
5. Async-safety: the pooled tenant is for non-async modules only unless you prove otherwise; say how misuse from an async module is rejected loudly.
6. The isolation proof: the exact mutation-test shape (a test that leaves data behind in every class: tenant tables, sequences, public rows; the next test must not see it), and a fail-safe so that if reset cannot prove cleanliness it falls back to a fresh clone rather than returning a dirty tenant.
7. Measurement plan satisfying the acceptance criteria: 5 before/after runs of the same partition, how to run them, what to record (run ids/wall time). Rollout: which modules adopt in this PR (start with the three named; justify any more), and what is explicitly out of scope.
8. Exact owned_modules for the implementer, and the list of existing tests that must stay green.
Constraints: no change to required CI check names; no paid runners; no production (lib/letflow) tenant-data path change; test/support only plus per-module opt-ins.
Complete the handoff per docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md (COMPLETED, real timestamps, artifacts_out listing the design file). Commit your design artefact and handoff completion to feature/WF03-ISS1042-20261012 and push. Do not edit handoffs/registry.json or handoffs/orchestrator.log.

REWORK ITERATION 1 (of max 3): CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR returned FAIL on your design (handoffs/WF03-ISS1042-20261012/step-02b-code-design-validator.json, full text of each finding is there; summary below). Revise lib/letflow/design/iss1042-pooled-tenant-fixture.md IN PLACE to resolve every finding, then complete this handoff (flip status to COMPLETED or FAILED as normal on finishing, with real completed_at and a fresh result.summary stating per finding F1..F6 and M-a..M-e where and how it is resolved). Commit and push to feature/WF03-ISS1042-20261012.
Fix the SPEC, do not argue it away: verify each claim against the files yourself (tenant_fixture.ex, tenant_template.ex, deps/ecto_sql sandbox source, lib/letflow/obs/alerts.ex:484, lib/letflow/login_discovery/dispatch.ex:56, store_test.exs) before answering.
Decision guidance from ORCH for the two BLOCKERS (you own the final design choice; deviate only with a stated reason):
- F1: define the structure fingerprint as a digest of DEFINITIONS (pg_get_triggerdef incl. tgenabled, pg_get_constraintdef, pg_get_indexdef, per-column type/default/nullability from pg_attribute/pg_attrdef, trigger function definitions, sequence parameters), or run the same dimensions as assert_clone_parity! in the runtime verify. Measure or bound its cost against the 3.6 ms probe / ~8 ms-per-table budget so the lever's gain survives; if the full digest is too slow per acquire, specify a cheap-always + full-on-recycle split and say why it is still sound. Add mutation classes for DISABLE TRIGGER and column/index/constraint alteration with unchanged counts.
- F2: restate INV-P1 precisely (what is proven, at which instant, what is NOT claimed); add an adopter audit rule for spawned/supervised/un-awaited processes that can touch the tenant schema, with an audit RESULT for each of the three adopter modules (a module that cannot be shown straggler-free must NOT be adopted in this PR); add a detection or mitigation for a late writer (e.g. a second probe immediately before return plus an end-of-test dirty-after check that fails the owning test loudly rather than silently corrupting the next one), and a mutation class that writes AFTER verify.
Also resolve: F3 pick ONE seed-restore mechanism (state the ISS-0842 ordering assumption); F4 rebuild path must re-run assert_schema_complete!, recapture baseline, re-snapshot the new Registration row, bump generation, and name the process that does it; F5 one rule: verify on every acquire including the first; F6 teardown first calls Sandbox.mode(Repo, :auto) (note the global check-in side effect). Minors: record OQ-1 answer B (test-process writes commit under :auto) with the sandbox-source evidence and drop the 'correct under both answers' claim, correct the counts in 1.2/7/5.1, specify attach_pool! ordering relative to setup blocks that call provisioned_tenant! (and make misordering fail loudly), give M2 one concrete table and sequence, say where pool_dirty_report/1 executes. owned_modules in this handoff's context are already corrected; make section 12 match.

FINDINGS (from validator):
- [BLOCKER] F1 structure fingerprint (design 4.2.1 / 4.3.1) is names plus COUNTS of indexes/constraints only, so DDL that preserves names and counts is invisible and never reset: ALTER TABLE .. DISABLE TRIGGER on audit_entries/repository_artifacts/artifact_versions (immutability triggers stay disabled for every later test in the module), ADD/DROP/ALTER COLUMN (type, default, NOT NULL), drop-and-recreate of an index or CHECK/FK constraint under the same name or with count unchanged, ALTER SEQUENCE INCREMENT/START, table/column comments. TRUNCATE does not undo any of it and the verify pass (4.3.5) compares the same weak fingerprint, so INV-P1 and 9.4 'never returns a dirty tenant' are false for this class. M8 covers only CREATE TABLE and DROP TRIGGER. Design must define the fingerprint as a digest of definitions (pg_get_triggerdef incl. tgenabled, pg_get_constraintdef, pg_get_indexdef, per-column type/default/nullability from pg_attribute/pg_attrdef, trigger function defs, sequence parameters) or run the same dimensions as assert_clone_parity! in the runtime verify, and add mutation classes for DISABLE TRIGGER and column/index/constraint alteration with unchanged counts.
- [BLOCKER] F2 late-writer / TOCTOU not closed, and a new leak class is unaudited. (a) 4.3.5 verifies in a separate transaction after COMMIT and the result is handed out with no lock or re-check, so any process still alive from the previous test can write between verify and the test's first use; INV-P1/9.4 ('no code path returns a slot whose cleanliness was not proven in that acquire') is true only at the verify instant and the doc presents it as unconditional. M10 simulates only a write between recycle_pool! and the next acquire, not one after verify. (b) A fresh tenant id per test made straggler processes harmless (they hit a dropped schema or a different id); a pooled id makes them corrupt the NEXT test. Section 6 audits only ETS/persistent_term holders. lib has fire-and-forget workers not considered: Task.Supervisor.start_child in lib/letflow/obs/alerts.ex:484 (Letflow.Obs.Alerts.TaskSupervisor) and lib/letflow/login_discovery/dispatch.ex:56 (LoginDiscovery.TaskSupervisor, async_nolink at :126), plus any un-awaited Task.async/Task.start in adopter modules (store_test.exs has Task.async at 338-339, 1151, 1162). Under Sandbox :auto their writes commit. Design must (i) restate INV-P1 precisely, (ii) add an adopter audit rule and result for spawned/supervised processes that can touch the tenant schema, (iii) specify a mitigation or a detection (e.g. second probe immediately before return plus an end-of-test dirty-after check that fails the owning test loudly), and add a mutation for a post-verify write.
- [MAJOR] F3 seed restore is specified two contradictory ways: 4.3.4.3 says INSERT INTO <clone>.<seed> SELECT * FROM tenant_template.<seed> (the do_clone steps 7-8 statements), while 4.4 says restore re-inserts from the baseline's captured rows as an Elixir term ('Resolved here'), and OQ-6 says fall back to the live template if the term is large. Re-inserting from a term requires re-encoding uuid/jsonb/timestamp columns of event_type_registry, and clone_baseline is declared @opaque with clone_state.seed_digests holding only {count, md5}, so the rows are not even in the stated shape. Pick one mechanism and state its ISS-0842 ordering assumption.
- [MAJOR] F4 rebuild path leaves state refresh unspecified. rebuild_clone_schema! (2.2) drops the schema, deletes the Registration row and re-clones; do_clone inserts a NEW Registration via Registration.changeset (new id, new provisioned_at/migrations_applied_at, tenant_template.ex:807-818), so registration_snapshot (3.2) is stale and the immediate verify (tenant_schemas row == snapshot, 4.3.5) would fail, causing a raise. The design never says that after a rebuild the worker re-runs assert_schema_complete!, recaptures baseline, re-snapshots the registration row, bumps generation, and which process runs it. M8/M9 expect 'generation incremented and clean' and cannot pass as written.
- [MAJOR] F5 internal contradiction on the first acquire: section 4 preamble says the first acquire of a :clean slot 'skips straight to hand-out' (no probe, no verify), while INV-P1 (13) and 9.4 say a pooled provisioned_tenant! returns only after a verify pass in that acquire. The probe costs 3.6 ms; state one rule (recommend verify always).
- [MAJOR] F6 pool teardown (3.4) and the module-end on_exit never set Sandbox.mode(Repo, :auto). DataCase sets {:shared, self()} per non-async test; if the module's last test did not call provisioned_tenant! (which is what flips to :auto) the on_exit/worker statements run with mode {:shared, dead_pid} or :manual and raise DBConnection.OwnershipError, leaving the schema to the reaper and failing the module. Specify that teardown first calls Sandbox.mode(:auto) (noting its global whole-pool check-in side effect, ISS-0113 9.1).
- [MINOR] M-a OQ-1 is resolvable now and the 'correct under both answers' claim is not true for section 9 under answer A. From deps/ecto_sql/lib/ecto/adapters/sql/sandbox.ex only explicit Sandbox.checkout/2 runs post_checkout begin (lines 544-551, 658); Manager auto-checkouts under :auto are not wrapped, and DataCase's {:shared, self()} -> fixture :auto is a mode change that checks in the DataCase connection (ISS-0113 9.2-9.3). Test-process writes therefore commit (answer B), consistent with the measured 41 ms DROP SCHEMA teardown (a no-op DROP would be ~1 ms). Under A, 9.2's 'mutate, recycle, assert pristine' would fail (uncommitted rows seen only by the test process, row locks block the worker TRUNCATE until lock_timeout). Record answer B in the design and drop the 'both' claim. identity_id_hardening_test.exs:454 comment 'DDL rolls back' is stale.
- [MINOR] M-b factual: design 1.2 says 52 test files use PlatformTenantFixture.three_tenants!; actual: 52 files reference PlatformTenantFixture, 27 reference three_tenants! (grep). Design 7 says '22+ template: :replay sites (29 files with the literal)'; actual: 29 occurrences in 14 files (two of those files are test/specs/*.md, one is test/support/tenant_fixture.ex).
- [MINOR] M-c factual: expected_tenant_tables/0 has 49 entries (tenant_fixture.ex:127-177), plus the separately created schema_migrations = 50 CREATE TABLE (LIKE) statements; the design's '50 x CREATE TABLE (LIKE ...)' is correct as statements, but the diagnosis label '50 expected_tenant_tables' is not. Section 5.1's informative public-table list omits public.secrets (tenant_id uuid, no FK, caught only by rule (b)) and event_history_retirement_outcomes (FK to tenants, on_delete :nothing).
- [MINOR] M-d handoff dispatch drift for ORCH: context.owned_modules omits store_test.exs, the new test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_pool_test.exs, docs/issues/ISS-1042.yaml and docs/anti-patterns.md that design 12.1 requires, and lists tenant_fixture_test.exs which the design makes conditional. started_at was null at claim; left null per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL 1.2.
- [MINOR] M-e minor under-specification: attach_pool! must run before any setup that calls provisioned_tenant! (identity_id_hardening_test.exs:49 calls three_tenants! from setup; wrong order silently takes the default path or, because attach resets the claim counter, hands {shape,0} out twice); M2 names 'definition_sequence/events global seq' as an example instead of one concrete table and sequence; where pool_dirty_report/1 executes (test process vs worker) is unstated.
acceptance_criteria: Instrumented measurement: clone time per test, tables per clone, share of total test time (numbers quoted)
One lever implemented with before/after wall time of the test phase (5 runs each, run ids)
Isolation proof: a test leaving data behind does not leak into the next test (mutation test)
No change to required check names; no paid runners

result.summary: Rework 1 of lib/letflow/design/iss1042-pooled-tenant-fixture.md, revised in place. F1 (BLOCKER): structure fingerprint is now a definitional digest D (4.2: pg_get_triggerdef incl. tgenabled, pg_get_constraintdef, pg_get_indexdef, per-column type/default/nullability/identity/collation, trigger function defs, sequence params, policies, rules, types, ext stats, inheritance, comments, owner/ACL), run on every detect and verify pass; drift is never repaired in place, always rebuild (INV-P10). Cost MEASURED against letflow_test tenant_template: 12.4-17.2 ms warm, 995 rows (1.1), so no cheap/full split; new mutations M8a/b, M15-M21 (DISABLE TRIGGER, column/index/constraint/sequence/comment/function alteration with unchanged counts, with a teeth check). F2 (BLOCKER): INV-P1 restated precisely (9.4, 13) with named residual risk RR-1; adopter audit rule 6.2 with per-module RESULT (all three straggler-free, grep-verified incl. obs/alerts.ex:484 and login_discovery/dispatch.ex:56 reachability, StoreTest Tasks all awaited); mitigations fence A (4.3.1), final guard with one re-reset then raise (4.3.7), end-of-test fence failing the owning test (3.6); mutations M13a/b/c (post-verify, persistent, post-guard containment) and M14 (straggler at end). A module that cannot be audited is dropped from the PR (11.3, INV-P11). F3: single seed mechanism = re-copy from live tenant_template; baseline holds only count+md5; ISS-0842 assumption stated, violation self-heals via verify-fail rebuild (4.4); OQ-6 withdrawn. F4: rebuild is run by the pool worker: rebuild_clone_schema!, assert_schema_complete!, recapture baseline, re-snapshot registration and tenant rows, generation+1, then normal proof (4.6, 3.2). F5: one rule, every acquire runs fence+detect+[reset+verify]+final guard including the first; status is informational (4.0, INV-P12). F6: teardown first calls Sandbox.mode(:auto) with the global check-in side effect noted (3.4); worker-routed APIs do the same (2.1). M-a: OQ-1 resolved as answer B with sandbox.ex evidence, 'correct under both' claim withdrawn (1.3). M-b: counts corrected (52 files reference PlatformTenantFixture, 27 call three_tenants!; 29 template: :replay occurrences in 14 files; 455 test files) (1.2, 7). M-c: 49 expected tables + schema_migrations = 50 statements; secrets and event_history_retirement_outcomes added to 5.1. M-d: section 12.1 matches; flagged for ORCH that the dispatched owned_modules path test/letflow/store_test.exs does not exist, real path test/letflow/definitions/store_test.exs. M-e: attach_pool! must be first setup, misordering and double attach raise (3.1, M22); M2 uses events_global_seq_seq via nextval; pool_dirty_report/1 etc execute in the pool worker (2.1). Design only, no implementation code.

issues.description: Dispatched context.owned_modules lists test/letflow/store_test.exs which does not exist; real file is test/letflow/definitions/store_test.exs. Design 12.1 uses the real path; ORCH should correct the ELIXIR-DEV dispatch.

Digest cost was measured on tenant_template (read-only, letflow_test on the letflow-3 docker Postgres), not on a live clone, and the pg_stat_activity end fence false-positive rate is unmeasured; both are OQ-8 for the implementer.

result.next_action: Re-dispatch CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR step 02b (rework iteration 1 re-validation); on PASS dispatch ELIXIR-DEV with owned_modules from design 12.1.
